item.text: I’ll apply the supplied series-continuity skill and check the draft against the commit receipt and the scheduled entry.

### LinkedIn draft

I committed a reusable checklist.

A checklist gives recurring work a starting point. The question is how much to standardize and where to leave room for judgment.

What’s one step you’d put on a checklist, and one you’d leave to the person doing the work?

### Private review note

| Item | Evidence and limits |
|---|---|
| Previous entry | Scheduled. The supplied text announces the intended checklist. Publication is unverified, and no observation timestamp or account receipt was supplied. The draft stands on its own. |
| Public claim | “I committed a reusable checklist” maps to the included commit receipt, which confirms the owner’s action and the artifact. The receipt establishes the commit. Readiness, adoption, and impact remain unverified. |
| Continuity | The draft moves from announcing the checklist to discussing what belongs on one. The second paragraph states a general principle and poses a question. The final question is the sole CTA. |
| Disclosure and review | The case permits the commit fact in the draft. The separate private ledger stays out of public copy. The proof-brief workflow and sibling drafting and voice workflows were unavailable. I checked the claim directly against the supplied receipt and used neutral wording because no owner voice sample was supplied. Owner review is pending. |
